chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Friday washing, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is obligatory during the journey and during residing, except that it is exempted for the women during the journey due to the scarcity of the water'.

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The major washing (from sexual impurity) is an obligation, and the washing of the menstruating woman when she is clean is an obligation, and the washing of the woman with inter-period bleeding is an obligation when she inserts with the rag, and the blood exceeds the rag, so upon her is the washing for every two prayers, and for the dawn prayer, a washing. And if the rag suffices for the blood, so upon her is the washing once every day, and the ablution for every prayer'.
And the washing for post-childbirth bleeding is an obligation, and washing for the child birth is an obligation.

And washing of the deceased is an obligation, and washing for visitation is an obligation, and washing for entering the House is an obligation, and washing for the supplication for rain is an obligation.

And washing in the first night of a month of Ramadan is recommended, and the washing of the night of the twenty-first, and the washing of the night of the twenty-third is a Sunnah, do not neglect these. For the Night of Pre-determination is hoped for in one of these.
And washing for the day of Eid al-Fitr and washing for the day of the Sacrifice is a Sunnah, I do not like it to be neglected, and washing for the Istikhara.
It is the recommended deed regarding the washing of the three nights from a month of Ramadan – the night of the nineteenth, and twenty-first, and the twenty-third.
ai.seo_question: What are the obligatory and recommended ritual washings (ghusl) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi systematically categorizes ritual washings (ghusl) into obligatory (wajib) and recommended (mustahabb) acts, highlighting the juristic nuance in applying concessions (rukhas) such as permitting women to skip Friday ghusl during travel due to water scarcity. It further details specific obligations for major impurity, menstruation, and post-childbirth, while emphasizing the spiritual significance of washings for specific nights in Ramadan, particularly those associated with Laylat al-Qadr.
